messages:
Jordan: Pushing this thread — noticed a ~30% tail-latency regression on llama-2-13b-quant after last night's kernel picker change. Repro with our chat template that prepends a long system prompt + special tokens.
Alyssa: when did it start?
Jordan: after the auto-rope-scale kernel heuristic landed (deploy 2026-03-16 03:12 UTC). infra-bot shows the deploy: https://ci.redwood.local/deploys/2026-03-16/abc123
Mike: can you paste the perf profile (flamegraph or short stack)?
Jordan: quick trace from the canary:
```
GPU timeline: kernel_picker -> choose_byte_fallback (score=0.62) -> byte_fallback_kernel (slow path)
KV cache stats: lookup_hits=1420 lookup_misses=384 (miss spike during first 200 tokens)
Batching: continuous_batching_disabled for 14% of requests in window
P95 latency: 220ms -> baseline 160ms
```
Jordan: interestingly, tokenizer shows the conversation template emits extra multi-byte sequences for BOS/EOS in some locales (byte-length variance).
Alyssa: that can push sequence chunking and ROPE offset calculation different -> kernel selector moves into a different bin. Byte-fallback path currently disables some prefetched KV heuristics.
Nora: hypothesis: the combination of (1) rope scaling changing token index mapping and (2) byte-fallback flag toggling causes the kernel_score to dip under the threshold and pick the slow kernel.
Sam: I ran a small canary modifying kernel threshold from 0.6 -> 0.8 on canary-2: P95 dropped from 220ms -> 150ms for 1k internal requests, and continuous batching re-enabled for the majority. Tail still has spikes for very long prompts.
Alyssa: what about throughput/cost?
Sam: throughput down ~5% on the canary but unit GPU time decreased due to fewer fallback executions, so cost per output token improved slightly.
Jordan: minimal repro case attached: uses chat-template with system block containing long unicode emojis and a trailing custom <assistant> token marker that the tokenizer encodes as 2 bytes.
Mike: can we short-term whitelist the chat templates that cause this? Also add a metric to detect when kernel_picker chooses fallback more than 5% vs baseline.
Nora: long-term: kernel_picker should fold in tokenizer-aware heuristics — if BOS/EOS or special-token byte-lengths differ from model baseline, bias away from fallback unless KV warmup counters are low.
Jordan: quick patch suggestion (kernel_picker.cc):
```
if (tokenizer_meta.multibyte_specials && score < fallback_bias) {
  score += tokenizer_meta.rope_alignment_bonus; // prefer rope-aware kernel
}
```
Sam: I opened PR 1979012345-kernel-picker-special-token-bias with unit+perf tests. Ran microbench: 1.15x improvement on these templates.
infra-bot: canary deployed to canary-2 cluster (id: canary-2-20260316-xyz) — smoke results: p95 145ms, p99 320ms.
Alyssa: good. Let's also add a short-lived alert in the console: metric kernel_selector.fallback_rate grouped by model+prompt_template. If fallback_rate delta > 3% for 10m -> page on-call.
Mike: agree. Also we should add a tokenizer regression test that simulates multibyte special tokens and validates kernel_selection stays consistent across rope-scaling modes.
Nora: will add the test to eng/runtime/tests/tokenizer_compat_suite.
Jordan: filed an incident note in #incidents and linked the PR. If the canary looks stable after 2 hours, we roll to staging.
Sam: rolling to staging now.
Alyssa: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. If it reappears, tag me and @infra-bot will capture full deploy+profile artifacts.
Jordan: thanks — tracking this under the perf regression card.
